as_told.title: Elizondo says he has seen the Big Sur video

plain: A test film from the 1960s, shot near Big Sur on the California coast, is said to show a UFO knocking down a dummy nuclear warhead, and Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office studying unexplained aerial reports, says he has seen it. The researcher Robert Hastings, who has spent years interviewing military veterans about UFOs near nuclear weapons, tells the fullest version on the show. Hastings says he got an email from Kurt McConnell, a Senate staffer, who had driven Elizondo to an interview with AARO, the Pentagon's UFO investigation office. On the drive back, McConnell wrote, Elizondo told him that he had told Sean Kirkpatrick, then AARO's head, that he had seen "the Big Sur film, the shootdown of a dummy nuclear warhead by a UFO." Hastings also brings in Bob Jacobs, a former Air Force officer whose name is tied to the film. Michels repeats the simpler claim twice, saying that Elizondo "said he saw that footage", and both times he leaves out Kirkpatrick and McConnell. The story matters because it would mean a film like this still exists and that the official in charge of looking for it was told about it.
